messages.text: Hamilton defends Ferrari amid ‘doom and gloom’ criticism

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari's season can still rank as a "huge achievement" if they finish in the top three of the Drivers' Championship, asking critics to "look at the positives" of the team's year despite recent setbacks.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver sets sights on George Russell in F1 championship amid defence of team's season | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver sets sights on George Russell in F1 championship amid defence of team's season "I think it's also just having to think about where we were last year and where we've come to this year," says Lewis Hamilton on Ferrari's fading title challenge; watch Thursday's practice sessions for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix at 9.30am and 1pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Wednesday 23 September 2026 15:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton says he believes the team can make improvements as he strives for 'cleaner' weekends. Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari's season can still rank as a "huge achievement" if they finish in the top three of the Drivers' Championship, asking critics to "look at the positives" of the team's year despite recent setbacks. Hamilton and Ferrari's hopes of winning this years world title have faded in recent races, with the Briton not finishing on the podium since the British Grand Prix at the start of July. A first race retirement of the season last time out in Madrid saw third-placed Hamilton fall over 100 points back on championship-leading Kimi Antonelli for the first time this season, with the seven-time champion all-but conceding the title. messages.text: Hadjar to remain at Red Bull for 2027

metadata.summary: Red Bull have confirmed Isack Hadjar will remain as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 Formula 1 season.
metadata.content: Isack Hadjar confirmed as Max Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate for 2027 Formula 1 season ahead of Azerbaijan Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Isack Hadjar confirmed as Max Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate for 2027 Formula 1 season ahead of Azerbaijan Grand Prix Isack Hadjar has extended his contract at Red Bull for another year and will be Max Verstappen's team-mate for a second season in 2027; watch Thursday's practice sessions for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix at 9.30am and 1pm, live on Sky Sports F1 By Nigel Chiu in Baku Wednesday 23 September 2026 14:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Isack Hadjar admits he's unsure of the new contract extension details and if he'll remain at Red Bull beyond 2027, but hopes his driving will do the talking Red Bull have confirmed Isack Hadjar will remain as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 Formula 1 season. Hadjar stepped up to Red Bull at the start of this year after an impressive debut campaign with Racing Bulls in 2025 but has missed the last three rounds due to a wrist injury he suffered during last month's summer break . But the 21-year-old is now fit enough to drive and is back at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which takes place on Saturday - live on Sky Sports F1 . Arteta has overseen a total transformation of the club since his appointment in 2019. Arsenal, 10th in the Premier League table when he took over, were in a state of drift. metadata.summary: Manchester United have announced record revenues for 2026, despite not competing in European competition last season.
metadata.content: Man Utd: Red Devils announced record revenues in 2026 despite not playing European football | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man Utd: Red Devils announced record revenues in 2026 despite not playing European football Man Utd's revenue is up from £666.5m in 2025, but the club have lost £43m over the course of the year; the club recorded an operating profit having recorded a loss last year; land for a new 100,000-seater stadium has also been confirmed Callum Bishop Football Journalist Wednesday 23 September 2026 13:14, UK Manchester United have announced record revenues for 2026, despite not competing in European competition last season. In their latest report, figures show that United recorded a revenue of £677.6m for the fiscal year, up from the previous record of £666.5m in 2025. However, the club has recorded a pre-tax loss of £43m over the course of the year, up from £33m . They also recorded a operating profit of £22.6m , having generated a loss of £18.4m last year, which is credited to 'the benefits of operating cost and headcount reductions previously implemented, combined with improved Premier League performance.' The Red Devils secured a third-place finish in the Premier League last season, largely thanks to the turnaround under then interim boss Michael Carrick, who won 11 of his 16 games in charge during the second-half of the campaign. messages.text: Teenager denies sending racist message to England defender Carter

metadata.summary: A teenager has denied sending a message containing a racial slur to England footballer Jess Carter during last year's Women's European Championship.
metadata.content: Jess Carter: Teenager denies sending racist message to England defender during Euro 2025 | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jess Carter: Teenager denies sending racist message to England defender during Euro 2025 Aaryan Aggarwal, 19, denied sending a racist message to England defender Jess Carter during Euro 2025; the teenager was charged with sending a message over a public network that was offensive, indecent, obscene or menacing; Warning: this article contains offensive language Wednesday 23 September 2026 12:59, UK Image: A teenager has pleaded not guilty to sending a racist message to England defender Jess Carter A teenager has denied sending a message containing a racial slur to England footballer Jess Carter during last year's Women's European Championship. Aaryan Aggarwal, 19, appeared at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court on Wednesday charged with sending a message over a public network that was offensive, indecent, obscene or menacing. Prosecutor Grace Court told the hearing that Carter received the message on July 17 last year, which was the day England beat Sweden in their quarter-final. Aggarwal is accused of telling the footballer: "Well done stupid ugly ******". The defendant pleaded not guilty to the offence during Wednesday's hearing. A trial date was fixed for October 3 next year at Cambridge Magistrates' Court.
